claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 6265: "The semantics of the cookie-value are not defined by this document." cookie.md: a ClaimsPrincipal "is serialized and stored in the cookie" (self-contained value in a cookie); "Once a cookie is created, the cookie is the single source of identity."

app-state.md: "The in-memory cache provider stores session data in the memory of the server where the app resides. In a server farm scenario: Use sticky sessions to tie each session to a specific app instance ... A better approach is to use a Redis, SQL Server, or Azure Postgres distributed cache". distributed.md: distributed data "Survives server restarts and app deployments." / "Doesn't use local memory."

cookie.md (same self-contained model): "Once a cookie is created, the cookie is the single source of identity." ... "Validating the cookie on every request mitigates the risk of revoked users accessing the app." (extra per-request check against stored data). Stage-1 JwtBearer validation has no such check (claim 4). Lesson wording 'the kind of store tokens were meant to avoid' stays within this claim.

app-state.md: "Session data is deleted either when the ISession.Clear implementation is called or when the session expires." and "If a cookie is received for an expired session, a new session is created that uses the same session cookie."
Conditional judgment with the condition stated in the sentence ("When ending a login immediately matters more than avoiding a store"); follows from claims 9 and 10. Not opinion-as-fact.

RFC 6750 (WebFetch summary) 2.1: "When sending the access token in the 'Authorization' request header field defined by HTTP/1.1, the client uses the 'Bearer' authentication scheme to transmit the access token." 1.2: bearer token = "any party in possession of the token (a 'bearer') can use the token". Lesson: '`Bearer` just labels what follows as a token' - consistent.

Live round 3: `docker compose restart api` then the step-2 curl with the same token, one try per ~1 s: 502 502 502 200. Caddyfile @ stage-1 `handle /api/v1/* { reverse_proxy api:8080 }` - Caddy answers while the upstream is down. donhang-db stayed 'Up 2 hours (healthy)'.

docker-compose.yml api.environment: `Jwt__SigningKey: "${JWT_SIGNING_KEY}"`; Program.cs reads `builder.Configuration["Jwt:SigningKey"]` before Build(). configuration/index.md: "A double underscore (`__`) is supported by all platforms and is automatically converted into a colon (`:`) when the configuration is read by the app." Value comes from .env (dev-secrets.sh), unchanged across restart.

Live round 3: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders` (no -H) -> 401; with Bearer -> 200. Output is the status code only. OrdersController.List is [Authorize] [HttpGet].

issues.text: Keyed option a asserts a remaining lifetime the context does not give. The context says someone 'got hold of their login token an hour ago' - that dates the theft, not the issue time. The token may have been issued hours earlier, so 'roughly seven hours away' is not derivable and can be false; a careful reader can reject the only keyed answer.
issues.quote: it will be accepted until its eight-hour lifetime runs out, roughly seven hours away.
issues.fix: Either (1) context en: 'A customer of Đơn Hàng logged in an hour ago, and someone else copied that login token right away.' (vi to match), or (2) option a en: 'Support has no way to stop just this one token today; it will be accepted until eight hours after it was issued.' (vi: '...cho tới tám giờ sau lúc được cấp.'). Keep explanation.correct consistent.

issues.text: Literally false: the API does hold the key in memory once it has read it (Program.cs keeps it in `signingKey`). The intended point is that the key is not created inside the process and so is not lost on restart.
issues.quote: The signing key doesn't live in the API's memory either:
issues.fix: Replace with: 'The signing key isn't made up inside the API process either:' (rest of sentence unchanged). Claim 14 already covers it.

issues.text: `curl`, `docker compose` and `scripts/up.sh` are tool names not in my known_vocab. Each step now says in plain words what the command does ('log in', 'prints only the status code', 'Restart only the API process'), so I can copy them and still follow the experiment; I just don't know the tools themselves. Not blocking.
issues.quote: Restart only the API process, leaving the database running: `docker compose restart api`.
issues.fix: Optional: in step 1, after '(`scripts/up.sh`)', add 'the script that starts the API and its database'. No other change needed.

issues.text: `Jwt` in `Jwt__SigningKey` is an unknown acronym, and `docker-compose.yml` is a file I've never been told about. The sentence's point (the key comes from outside the process, at startup, so it's the same after a restart) is clear without them.
issues.quote: the API reads it at startup from the `Jwt__SigningKey` environment variable that `docker-compose.yml` passes in.
issues.fix: Replace 'that `docker-compose.yml` passes in' with 'that `docker-compose.yml` (the file that starts the example system) passes in'. Leave `Jwt` for the next lesson.

issues.text: Step 2 uses `<token>` as a placeholder; I guess I paste the copied value there (angle brackets included or not?). The sentence 'Without the -H ... part it prints 401' also reads as a fact, and I'm not sure whether I'm meant to run it.
issues.quote: Call `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` — it prints only the status code.
issues.fix: Add 'replacing `<token>` (brackets included) with the value you copied' and change 'Without the `-H ...` part it prints `401`' to 'Run it once without the `-H ...` part: it prints `401`.'

issues.text: Correct option a is still the longest and the only one that hedges honestly ('no way... today'); b-d are confident promises. I could pick it by tone. I can also reason it out from section 4 and 5, so this is only a cue, not a gap.
issues.quote: Support has no way to stop just this one token today; it will be accepted until its eight-hour lifetime runs out, roughly seven hours away.
issues.fix: Drop ', roughly seven hours away' from a, or add a short reason clause to b and d so lengths match.

issues.text: Correct option c is the longest of the four and the only one with two reasons joined by 'and'. The reasoning is clearly available from section 6, so this is only a length cue.
issues.quote: False, because what decides the model is a server-side lookup, and a cookie can hold a token just as well as an id.
issues.fix: Shorten c to 'False: a cookie can hold a token that the server checks without looking anything up.'
